# Revision 10: the security category as an input, counting convention EVERY t, the SG26 hash term on every row, classical hash basis attack-rule (generated by `uv run yugen-soundness --rev7`)

Tree of 20,000 proofs; union bound; no grinding; unique decoding for certified rows; true rates; spBCS (Sharp-Grubbs, ePrint 2026/2615, Theorem 6.6). Sizes are estimates (E) anchored on measured proofs (M): A's masked leaf 688,180 B (row 6, 64-byte salts), A's node 875,309 B, B's form-T leaf 583,680 B (32-byte salts), B's node 538,272 B (2^23 words); non-opening bytes scale with the field's element size.

## Derivation of the targets from NIST-CfP Section 4.A.5 (pages 16 to 18)

| Category | NIST's requirement (reference attack) | Classical gates (p. 18) | Quantum gates x MAXDEPTH (p. 18) | kappa_C (oracle calls) | Gates an evaluation implied | Grover overhead implied | kappa_Q | G a round | Digest, attack rule | Digest, proven rule (book term 3.5 t^2 / 2^lambda, SUPERSEDED) | Digest, proven rule (SG26 hash term, tree, c' = 2,401) | Book need, A (k = 599; non-default) | Book need, B (k = 600; non-default) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | key search on AES128 | 2^143 | 2^170 | 128 | 2^15 | 2^42 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 264 | 288 | 152.52 | 152.52 |
| 2 | collision search on SHA256/ SHA3-256 | 2^146 | not given | 128 | 2^18 | - | 64 | 128 | 256 | 264 | 288 | 152.52 | 152.52 |
| 3 | key search on AES192 | 2^207 | 2^233 | 192 | 2^15 | 2^41 | 96 | 192 | 384 | 392 | 416 | 216.52 | 216.52 |
| 4 | collision search on SHA384/ SHA3-384 | 2^210 | not given | 192 | 2^18 | - | 96 | 192 | 384 | 392 | 416 | 216.52 | 216.52 |
| 5 | key search on AES 256 | 2^272 | 2^298 | 256 | 2^16 | 2^42 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 520 | 544 | 280.52 | 280.52 |

Revision 9: the last two columns are the book's needs, NON-DEFAULT (t >= k_q). The default need (every t) is kappa_C + 1 + log2 N + log2(1 + k_q) at each row's own k_q (SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2), Definitions H.3, H.4; docs/decision-qrom-counting.md): 157.0 to 158.8 bits at category 1, printed with each row.

Revision 10 (finding R9-1): the proven digest rule is taken from the hash term of SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2) itself, c' (t + k_q)^2 / 2^(8b) per proof summed over the tree: 8b >= 2 kappa_C + 1 + log2(N c') (k_q negligible against 2^kappa_C), whole bytes. The book column (3.5 t^2 / 2^lambda, counted once for the tree: the source of the former '126.6 proven classical bits' and '264') is kept as a record.

Condition Q's per-round need (Theorem 6.6 (2) IOP term, C1 = 6, N = 20,000): cat1 145.87; cat2 145.87; cat3 209.87; cat4 209.87; cat5 273.87 bits; condition C binds at every category.

## cat1 (as built: D-b salts, SQ-48 BLAKE3): digest 256 bits, salts 64 B (proof) / 64 B (leaf), GF(2^256), tree hashes Keccak-256 (A) / BLAKE3 (B)

### The hash term of SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2) (revision 10, finding R9-1)

Per proof c' (t + k_q)^2 / 2^256 (ROM) and 6 c' (t + k_q)^3 / 2^256 (QROM), summed over N = 20,000 proofs; b = 32 bytes is the length of every digest the transcript writes (SG26 Section I.1: challenge-input keys, leaf and node digests, the written-back stream prefix; at category 1 Keccak-256 keys and trees with SHAKE256 streams in A, SHA-256 keys, BLAKE3 trees and SHAKE256 streams in B; this profile's trees: Keccak-256 (A), BLAKE3 (B)). Classical: the largest kappa with the tree term <= t / 2^(kappa + 1) for every 1 <= t <= 2^kappa (binding at t = 2^kappa). QROM: the query count at which the tree term reaches 1/2. Revision 10.2: the tree's classical hash level is Theorem TE' of docs/lemma-tree-extraction.md (the hash part taken once for the tree, c'_max (t + N k_q,max)^2 / 2^256), under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1; the per-proof union form is printed beside it as the comparison and is what the proven-basis check uses (the lower figure).

| System | Rows | c' (range) | Classical, proof | Classical, tree, Theorem TE' (under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1) | Classical, tree, per-proof union (comparison) | kappa_C | Classical shortfall, TE' / union | Digest for a classical tree at kappa_C, TE' / union (bits) | QROM, proof | QROM, tree | kappa_Q | QROM margin | Classical hash part judged by | Verdict, classical | Verdict, quantum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 20 | 2,157 to 2,397 | 121.89 | 121.89 | 114.74 | 128 | 6.11 / 13.26 | 272 / 288 | 80.40 | 75.63 | 64 | +11.63 | attack-rule | meets on condition H's attack rule (digest 256 >= 256); NOT as a proven bound | meets (tree derived under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1) |
| B | 4 | 2,401 to 2,401 | 121.89 | 121.89 | 114.74 | 128 | 6.11 / 13.26 | 272 / 288 | 80.40 | 75.63 | 64 | +11.63 | attack-rule | meets on condition H's attack rule (digest 256 >= 256); NOT as a proven bound | meets (tree derived under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1) |

### The tree's QROM figures: per-proof union (claimed) and the one-table form of Proposition TE-Q' (revision 10.2)

Every figure below is derived under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1 (recursion heuristic C2, not a proven QROM theorem; no unconditional QROM figure exists for a tree whose inner proofs are witnesses), and in addition on SG26 Theorem I.16 (1) (a preprint), H-BIND and Lemma QC (refereed, pass). The project claims the per-proof union, the lower figure.

## Salt floors from a zero-knowledge target (pool of 2^20 leaf proofs; each figure excludes Q eps_hvzk)

Leaf salt floor: the leaf term alone (independent of t). Proof salt floor: the salt term at t = 2^kappa_Q of the privacy category (t counts hash queries before the last proof; Theorem 6.6 (3)).

| 2^-96 | 67 / 67 | 83 / 83 | 99 / 99 | 46 | 54 | 62 |
| 2^-128 | 75 / 75 | 91 / 91 | 107 / 107 | 54 | 62 | 70 |

Counts (n_pos, leaf bytes) are category 1's; at larger counts n_pos changes by under one bit (leaf salt floors move by at most one byte).

### Refusals (hard failures, `OutsideRegime`)

- a fold line of message dimension 1 without Lemma 3.3: refused: node at rate 1/8: X fold 28 has message dimension 1 (log_terminal_dim = 0); DKT26 Theorem 4.4 excludes D = 0. Add DKT26 Lemma 3.3's term (dimension_one='lemma33') or choose log_terminal_dim >= 1
- Haboeck's route: refused: Haboeck's route is not available for system B as built (binius-johnson-row.md 0.1: gaps G-1, G-3, G-6); only 'ud' and 'dkt' are computed
- m = 2: refused: m = 2 < 3: outside the Johnson regime of binius-johnson-row.md 2.2 (and DKT26 (36) m >= 3)
- m missing: refused: the Johnson regime needs m
- m not an integer: refused: m = 10.0: the Johnson parameter must be an integer >= 3
- D > n - 2: refused: D = 15 > n - 2 = 14: outside DKT26 Theorem 4.4's hypothesis 1 <= D <= n - 2
- log_terminal_dim above the message log: refused: log_terminal_dim = 29: outside 0 .. 28 (the message log2 of the node's largest level)
- log_terminal_dim negative: refused: log_terminal_dim = -1: outside 0 .. 28 (the message log2 of the node's largest level)
- a Johnson threshold above the unique-decoding one (m = 1 is refused first; rate 1/2, m = 3): refused: m = 3, rate 1/2: the Johnson threshold (1 + 1/(2m)) sqrt(rho) is not below the unique-decoding threshold (1 + rho)/2
- the same node with DKT26 Lemma 3.3 added: X fold 28 (message dimension 1): count 52, 250.30 bits

### What "proven" and "certified" rest on (revision 10.2; docs/what-is-proven.md)

Every figure called proven, and every row labelled certified, rests on the random-oracle model and on the conditions below, some of them OWED, so in the terms of docs/what-is-proven.md it is conditional; every TREE figure (classical and quantum) is in addition conditional on the recursion heuristic C2, read as a joint probability (never a conditional one; equivalence tests do not discharge it), and none is an unconditional theorem. Conditions: (1) C2, the recursion heuristic (the event 'a child proof accepted by the in-circuit verifier and rejected by the native verifier' does not occur; NOT dischargeable by any random-oracle proof; excluded in practice by in-circuit / native verifier equivalence, a tested engineering property; it enters Theorem TE' at the child's acceptance and by keeping the node relation oracle-free); (2) K-A and K-B, OWED: the round-by-round KNOWLEDGE soundness of both IOPs outside the openings; (3) T-1, OWED from the builders: the transcripts' domain separation across systems (H-DS, injective encodings), their fit to Sharp-Grubbs Protocol 6.5, and the reported c' and k_q (until then c' and k_q are estimates, marked E); (3a) C-4, the level and proof-count binding in node statements: met by design, by search, NOT audited (an audit owed); (3b) H-BIND, collision resistance of the concrete statement-digest functions computed inside the node relations (a standard-model assumption, not an oracle property; it excludes SHAPE-VIOLATION and bounds the tree's node count); (4) the modelling assumptions MA-1 (Keccak-256 and SHAKE256 in A, SHA-256 and SHAKE256 in B, as one random oracle with four disjoint parts) and MA-2' (BLAKE3 derive_key, B's leaves and nodes, as that oracle's leaf and node parts); (5) Sharp-Grubbs, ePrint 2026/2615, Theorem 6.6 (2) and Theorem I.16 (1), (2): a PREPRINT; (6) Theorem TE' (docs/lemma-tree-extraction.md revision 3; revisions 1 and 2 refereed, pass with conditions; revision 3, with SHAPE-VIOLATION and Lemma TE.3, UNREFEREED); (7) Lemma QC (the continuation after a database measurement, from Chiesa-Manohar-Spooner, ePrint 2019/834, Lemma 3.2): refereed, pass (docs/qc-and-status-referee.md); (8) Theorem D (system B's repeated openings): refereed, pass with conditions. Candidate (Johnson-regime) rows rest in addition on DKT26 (Dao, Kominers, Thaler, ePrint 2026/2056), a PREPRINT, and are never certified. At category 1 (256-bit digests) the tree's classical hash level is 121.89 bits (Theorem TE', under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1); the per-proof union form, 114.74, is printed beside it and is the figure the proven-basis check uses; the tables give each profile's figures. The classical hash part is certified on condition H's attack rule unless the basis printed says proven.
